doc.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025

title: Collaborating with Donald Fagen on horn parts, including 'IGY'
summary: How Fagen dictated or delegated horn parts, and his solving of the B major to F minor pivot in 'IGY'.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Hm. Figuring out what would work. This — when I read your credits on here it says that you collaborated with Donald Fagen on the horn parts.
So I’m trying to imagine how that works. Do you sit and listen to the track and you both trade turns like humming something — or here’s a spot let’s put something in here?
What it mostly meant was he’d play it for me and sometimes he would actually dictate certain parts to me and other times he’d just say just fill this in with something good. You
know. For instance in the song “IGY” I think that’s the opening song [scats] in B. If I turn this up –
Yeah I can sort of hear that.

Oh okay. That’s all Donald. That’s Donald’s thing. But then it goes from B major, as it goes into the verse it has to pivot into F minor, an extremely remote modulation from five sharps to four flats. And he didn’t know how to get out of that line. So I figured out [scats]. That was me. You know pivot on the G sharp note, make in an A flat and then put a G natural next to it and then you’re indicating F minor, four flats. But that was the kind of weird stuff that was not that natural to him. And he used to say to me, “You know I could do this, I don’t really need you to do this except it would take me three months and it takes you half an hour. And he was right, he could have done it himself but I was faster. To me it was sort of like at the center of how I heard stuff and saw it, and for him he was writing all those great songs.
